text: Risk management is the process of identifying potential problems before they happen and planning how to deal with them. First, you need to identify risks, such as financial losses, delays, or safety issues. Once identified, you can create mitigation strategies to reduce the chance of these risks occurring. For example, a company might train staff to prevent accidents. However, not all risks can be avoided, so it is also important to have contingency plans. These are backup actions you will take if things go wrong, like using a different supplier if your main one fails. Finally, you must monitor the situation regularly. Risks can change over time, so reviewing your plans helps you stay prepared for new challenges.
